summary.en: The settlement of the Second Balkan War divided Ottoman Macedonia between Greece, Serbia and Bulgaria. Greece gained Epirus, most of Macedonia including Thessaloniki, and the northern Aegean islands. In two campaigns the kingdom had roughly doubled in both territory and population, and had absorbed a population that was not predominantly Greek speaking.

body_html.en:
The First Balkan War had driven the Ottoman Empire out of almost all of Europe by the spring of 1913, and the Treaty of London left the allies to divide the spoils. Bulgaria, which had done most of the fighting in Thrace, attacked its former allies in June to take Macedonia and was beaten within a month.

At Bucharest in August Greece kept everything its army had reached: Thessaloniki, which it had entered hours ahead of the Bulgarians in November 1912, Kavala, and the whole of southern Macedonia. Crete's union was confirmed and the eastern Aegean islands followed in 1914. The population of the state rose from about 2.7 to 4.8 million.
